extraction_warnings: PDF source uses 8-digit codes without dots (e.g., '88021100') and 6-digit subheading codes without dots (e.g., '880100'). Normalized to NNNN.NN.NN format (e.g., '8802.11.00') and NNNN.NN format (e.g., '8801.00') per project schema.

PDF table-chrome headers ('Main Notes', 'Sub-Heading Notes', 'Sl.No. Notes Notification Date Notification No', 'Product Description and Export Policy', 'Itc(hs) Code. Description Export Policy Policy Condition') were recognized as table chrome and EXCLUDED from the legal notes per extraction rules.

The PDF presents two distinct 'Main Notes' tables. The first table (Section XVII, VEHICLES, AIRCRAFT, VESSELS AND ASSOCIATED TRANSPORT EQUIPMENT) contains Notes 1-5 that apply to Section XVII as a whole (Chapters 86-89) — captured as section_notes. The second table (under the 'Chapter 88 Aircraft, Spacecraft, And Parts Thereof.' heading) contains Note 1 that is specific to Chapter 88 — captured as chapter_notes.

Heading 8803 ('Parts of goods of heading 8801 or 8802') is absent from this chapter PDF. Per the WCO HS 2022 nomenclature update, heading 8803 was deleted and its scope was merged into the new heading 8807 ('Parts of goods of heading 8801, 8802 or 8806'). Also, heading 8806 ('Unmanned aircraft') is new in the HS 2022 nomenclature. PDF correctly reflects HS 2022.

Tariff line 8801.00.11 ('Gliders and hang gliders') has no Export Policy value in the source PDF — the Export Policy and Policy Condition columns are blank for this code. Preserved as null; this is an apparent data gap in the source PDF (all other tariff lines in the chapter are 'Free').

Sub-Heading Notes in the source PDF reference sub-headings using a space-separator notation ('8802 11 to 8802 40', '8806 21 to 8806 24', '8806 91 to 8806 94'). Preserved verbatim — these correspond to subheadings 8802.11-8802.40 and 8806.21-8806.24 / 8806.91-8806.94 in the normalized NNNN.NN format.

Heading 8802 description in the PDF is presented in uppercase ('OTHER AIRCRAFT, EXCEPT UNMANNED AIRCRAFT OF HEADING 88.06 (FOR EXAMPLE, HELICOPTERS, AEROPLANES), SPACECRAFT (INCLUDING SATELLITES) AND SUBORBITAL AND SPACECRAFT LAUNCH VEHICLES'). Heading 8806 is also uppercase ('UNMANNED AIRCRAFT'). Heading 8807 is also uppercase ('PARTS OF GOODS OF HEADING 8801, 8802 OR 8806'). Preserved verbatim from the PDF case.

Section XVII Note 2 lists what is NOT 'parts and accessories' for Chapters 86-89. This is the same Section XVII Note 2 that applies to Chapter 87 (vehicles) — captured verbatim with exclusion sub-clauses (a) through (l).

Section XVII Note 3 ('References in Chapters 86 to 88 to "parts" or "accessories" do not apply to parts or accessories which are not suitable for use solely or principally with the articles of those Chapters.') is the principal-use rule for parts classification — captured verbatim as section_notes entry 3.

Section XVII Note 4 reference to 'Chapter 88' (sub-clause (c): 'aircraft specially constructed so that they can also be used as road vehicles are classified under the appropriate heading of Chapter 88.') is split across pages 1 and 2 of the PDF. Reconstructed verbatim by joining the page break.

The Section XVII Main Notes table has a 'Notification Date' column appearing BEFORE the 'Notification No' column in some rows of this PDF (column order reversed compared to other chapter PDFs). All values are empty for all section/chapter/sub-heading notes — null preserved.
The 'Export Policy' column for every tariff line in this chapter (where present) is 'Free'. No tariff lines are Restricted, Prohibited, or STE in this chapter PDF.
Unit-of-measure column is NOT shown in this chapter's PDF — unit field set to null for all tariff lines.

Subheading 8806.30 is absent from the PDF (the unmanned aircraft heading 8806 contains 8806.10, then 8806.21/22/23/24/29 for remote-controlled, then 8806.91/92/93/94/99 for 'Other'). Mirrors the official HS 2022 structure — no extraction gap.

Subheading 8802.50 is absent from the PDF — heading 8802 lists 8802.11, 8802.12, 8802.20, 8802.30, 8802.40, 8802.60 (spacecraft and suborbital). The 8802.50 slot is unused in HS 2022. Mirrors the official structure.

Heading 8803 (deleted in HS 2022) is referenced in Section XVII Note 3 as part of 'Chapters 86 to 88'. Parts of aircraft are now under 8807. No extraction action needed — note text preserved verbatim.

chapter_notes.text: For the purposes of this Chapter, the expression "unmanned aircraft" means any aircraft, other than those of heading 8801, designed to be flown without a pilot on board. They may be designed to carry a payload or equipped with permanently integrated digital cameras or other equipment which would enable them to perform utilitarian functions during their flight. The expression "unmanned aircraft", however, does not cover flying toys, designed solely for amusement purposes (heading 9503).

section_notes.text: This Section does not cover articles of heading 9503 or 9508 or bobsleighs, toboggans and the like of heading 9506.

The expressions "parts" and "parts and accessories" do not apply to the following articles, whether or not they are identifiable as for the goods of this Section: (a) joints, washers or the like of any material (classified according to their constituent material or in heading 8484) or other articles of vulcanised rubber other than hard rubber (heading 4016), (b) parts of general use, as defined in Note 2 to Section XV, of base metal (Section XV), or similar goods of plastics (Chapter 39), (c) articles of Chapter 82 (tools), (d) articles of heading 8306, (e) machines and apparatus of headings 8401 to 8479, or parts thereof, other than the radiators for the articles of this Section, articles of heading 8481 or 8482 or, provided they constitute integral parts of engines and motors, articles of heading 8483, (f) electrical machinery or equipment (Chapter 85), (g) articles of Chapter 90, (h) articles of Chapter 91, (ij) arms (Chapter 93), (k) luminaries and lighting fittings and parts thereof of heading 9405, or (l) brushes of a kind used as parts of vehicles (heading 9603).

References in Chapters 86 to 88 to "parts" or "accessories" do not apply to parts or accessories which are not suitable for use solely or principally with the articles of those Chapters. A part or accessory which answers to a description in two or more of the headings of those Chapters is to be classified under that heading which corresponds to the principal use of that part of accessory.

For the purposes of this Section: (a) vehicles specially constructed to travel on both road and rail are classified under the appropriate heading of Chapter 87, (b) amphibious motor vehicles are classified under the appropriate heading of Chapter 87, (c) aircraft specially constructed so that they can also be used as road vehicles are classified under the appropriate heading of Chapter 88.

Air-cushion vehicles are to be classified within this Section with the vehicles to which they are most akin as follows: (a) in Chapter 86 if designed to travel on a guide-track (hovertrains), (b) in Chapter 87 if designed to travel over land or over both land and water, (c) in Chapter 89 if designed to travel over water, whether or not able to land on beaches or landing - stages or also able to travel over ice. Parts and accessories of air-cushion vehicles are to be classified in the same way as those of vehicles of the heading in which the air-cushion vehicles are classified under the above provisions. Hovertrain track fixtures and fittings are to be classified as railway track fixtures and fittings, and signalling, safety or traffic control equipment for hovertrain transport systems as signalling, safety or traffic control equipment for railways.

chapter_subheading_notes.text: For the purposes of sub-headings 8802 11 to 8802 40, the expression "unladen weight" means the weight of the machine in normal flying order, excluding the weight of the crew and of fuel and equipment other than permanently fitted items of equipment.

For the purposes of sub-headings 8806 21 to 8806 24 and 8806 91 to 8806 94, the expression "maximum take-off weight" means the maximum weight of the machine in normal flying order, at take-off, including the weight of payload, equipment and fuel.
